decisions.action: audit clock enablement by resolving the DTB's flat clock cells against the driver's registered IDs, per provider domain
decisions.reason: 'the driver compiles and the symbol is on' says nothing about whether the provider can answer the board. Three tool bugs had to be fixed to make the number trustworthy, each of which would have produced a false all-clear or a false alarm: dtc -O dts prefixes nodes with their label ('pericfg: pericfg@10003000 {'), so a name-only regex lost the providers and made every reference look dangling; '#clock-cells' needs '#' in the property regex; multi-string compatibles print as one quoted string separated by \0 and must be split. Domain attribution also has to include mux/divider/factor tables, not just *_clks[], or topckgen reads as 5/65 registered when it is 65/65.

Vendor MT6768 PMIC-wrap map agrees with mainline's mt8183 table on all 43 comparable registers (0 differing) and with mt6765 on only 6 of 20 (RDDMY/HARB_HPRIO/MAN_CMD/WACS0_EN/INIT_DONE2/TIMER_EN/DCM all shifted). Offsets for every register pwrap_mt8183_init_soc_specific() writes were checked individually. MT6768 also has P2P/MD32 masters in its DTB, so that init applies.

Taken from the vendor's own MT6768 init (pwrap_hal.c:901,913) instead of MT8183's 0x3fa75/0xeef7ffff: the arbiter mask differs in bit 4 (which bus masters may reach the PMIC), so reusing MT8183's value would have been an invention with real consequences.

decisions.action: deliberate omission: PWRAP_CAP_DCM not set for mt6768
decisions.reason: MT6768 has DCM_EN/DCM_DBC_PRD at 0x1D0/0x1D8, which mt8183_regs does not describe; setting the cap would send the generic DCM path to offset 0. Cost is a missing debounce-counter diagnostic, not a wrong register write.

decisions.title: narrow B′ costed against measurements: the slot half lands alone, cmdqRecWrite lands with the GCE mailbox binding
decisions.context: After the published-series gate was clean and the repo synchronised (the condition decision 144 set), the record-layer design was measured rather than assumed: the four needed entry points, the vendor's actual opcode path (cmdqRecWrite -> cmdq_op_write_reg -> WRITE_S/WRITE_S_W_MASK + MASK, not cmdq_pkt_write), the bit-for-bit comparison of the vendor and mainline instruction words, the PA->subsys-id table (DT data under the gce node, already landed by 0070), and what cmdqBackup*Slot is backed by (a coherent buffer with the PA as handle, via cmdqCoreAllocWriteAddress; no GCE MMIO in the CPU path).
decisions.decision: (1) Land the backup-slot trio first and alone - CPU-visible pool + pa->va registry, ~120 lines, device for the DMA API obtained from the gce/syscon node without a mailbox channel. (2) Do NOT land cmdqRecWrite as a standalone slice: its only sane body is cmdq_pkt_write_s_value/_mask_value over a struct cmdq_pkt, and no pkt can exist until a mailbox provider binds the gce node (mainline 5.15 matches only mt8173/mt8183/mt6779/mt8192/mt8195-gce; our landed node is "mediatek,gce","syscon" with no #mbox-cells), so a record layer landed now would be either dead code or a silent-drop shim - the latter already rejected twice as fabrication. It lands with the binding slice. (3) Encodings: for any address the DT table resolves (all 12 landed module addresses resolve to id 1 or 2; the vendor DT marks pwm 0x1100e000 as 99 = CMDQ_SPECIAL_SUBSYS_ADDR itself), the vendor word and mainline's are identical: sop:5 at bits 16-20 == CMDQ_ARG_A_SUBSYS_MASK 0x001F0000, offset at 0-15, type bits at 21-23, op at 24-31, value at 32-63. The one place they differ is the ASSIGN-to-GPR fallback (vendor CMDQ_LOGIC_ASSIGN<<16 vs mainline reg_dst), which nothing landed needs - so it is left unimplemented rather than guessed. (4) New helper code goes in a new gated file under obj-$(CONFIG_MTK_CMDQ_DISP_RECORD) (default n) instead of growing mtk-cmdq-helper.c's body, keeping the mainline CMDQ stack coherent.
still_open_on_purpose: whether the GCE reaches the slot pool by PA or through M4U/SMI as IOVA (hardware/DT question; no landed code has the GCE write to a slot, so it does not block step 1)
whether MT6768 accepts mainline's LOGIC/ASSIGN bit layout (only needed with the fallback, i.e. with the not-in-table path)
how the gce node gains a mailbox provider: add #mbox-cells + a matching compatible (a device-DT/binding change, so it needs stock-handover evidence and the user's OK) or a port-local provider
consequences: the record layer is cheaper than the option list assumed: 0 new opcodes, and cmdqRecWrite becomes a 2-line adapter over functions already present in our tree
the mediatek,gce question is reframed from an MMIO ownership conflict (none exists today) into the reason the record half cannot be landed first
all of it recorded in report/l2-record-layer-design-bprime.md with file:line citations

decisions.title: 0088 lands the slot-pool half; the record-write half is confirmed to be a link-time-only dependency; and a test that passed before the behaviour it tested existed
decisions.context: Decision 146 set the split and ordered the slot half first, with cmdqRecWrite deferred until the GCE binding question is resolved from stock evidence and no speculative #mbox-cells/compatible/port-local provider is added. This round implemented, gated, published and reassessed that slice.
decisions.decision: (1) The slot trio landed as 0088 in the shape 146 predicted, with one measured correction: 146's 'device for the DMA API from the gce/syscon node without a mailbox channel' was NOT carried out - the vendor's own allocator (cmdqCoreAllocWriteAddress) never touches a device, it just alloc_pages() and hands out page_to_phys() as the handle, so the port does the same and no of_parse/parent-device lookup was invented. A provider that allocated through a device the vendor does not consult would have been the same kind of speculation 146 forbids. (2) Kconfig: the intent ('enable exactly when the display core is enabled') is served directly by keying the obj line on CONFIG_MTK_DISP_BRINGUP. A separate symbol plus `default MTK_DISP_BRINGUP` measured INERT against an explicit `# CONFIG_MTK_DISP_BRINGUP is not set` in .config (that is 0084-0086's dead-code mode, discovered from the other direction), and `select` propagates but cannot force off and defaults to y - a policy inversion for a default-n driver. Both were measured and both were rejected. (3) Reachability, reassessed from the callsites as 146 required: cmdqRecWrite is referenced 29 times at link time from 2 objects (ddp_mutex.o, ddp_rsz.o via ddp_reg.h's DISP_REG_* macros) - NOT the '2 refs' my own design note said, which conflated referencing objects with referencing callsites. 9 of the 11 T symbols those two objects define are used by ddp_manager.o, so the mutex layer is live inside the landed set, but the cmdqhandle it forwards is a parameter (ddp_manager.c:49/:415/:545) and nm -u finds 0 references to cmdqRecCreate/cmdqRecDestroy. So nothing in the landed set can execute a record today: the deferral costs a link, not a behaviour, and the next real consumer (ddp_dsi, deferred by decision 135) arrives with the DSI slice. (4) Harness lesson, and the reason the same bug pattern is now a rule here: [4b] 'pools adjacent' reported agreement while proving nothing, because stock and port shared one bump arena and the alias only reaches the NEXT pool - which then belonged to the other implementation, so both sides wrote a pool nobody asserted on. The case passed before the behaviour it was written to demonstrate occurred. Fix: allocate each side's pools contiguously and assert the observable (pool2[0]==0xE7E7 on both sides), not just stock==port. (5) Two comments in the landed source claimed more than was measured ('a real client would see the same pool contents', 'the vendor guard is kept'): both rewritten to say what was measured and to name the one divergence (stock's `s32 offset` truncates at >=2 GiB separation and can alias into a wrong pool; the port's `long` refuses, unreachable with low-DRAM alloc_pages but a deliberate divergence, recorded in the commit message rather than hidden).
decisions.still_open_on_purpose: cmdqRecWrite still has no provider and the record-write half of B' stays deferred: the binding question needs stock evidence (the 4.19 vendor gce node's #mbox-cells and any sibling sharing the syscon), not a port-local guess; the GCE reassessment changed the cost estimate, not the design. The vendor's out-of-range guard (cmdq_helper_ext.c:2163) stays unported because no landed caller reaches it, and that asymmetry is written down in the code, not just here. ddp_path's three record-API callsites, ddp_dsi, BDG and the panel-enable question are untouched.
consequences: 0088 published: 88 numbered .eml + cover; full-set am -> 1a7cf42b066c..., 0001-0087 prefix -> deba5bd29ec6..., both verified; cover tail regenerated (944 files, +119751/-2382) and its count fields corrected; MANIFEST 422 lines (421 at publish time, +1 from the header prefix correction later in the same round).

decisions.decision: Record, not choose. Measured: (a) stock MT6768 splits the roles - `gce` (mt6768.dts:1424) is `"mediatek,gce","syscon"` + the 31 subsys triples with NO #mbox-cells, while a separate `gce_mbox` node (:1601, `"mediatek,mt6768-gce"`, same reg/interrupts, `#mbox-cells = <3>`, `#gce-event-cells`/`#gce-subsys-cells`, `default_tokens`) is the mailbox provider, with a second `gce_mbox_svp` node (:1623) compiled only under the secure Kconfig `#if`; (b) stock's provider is the same file mainline has - its `cmdq_of_ids[]` (:2047) just contains `{mt6768-gce, gce_plat_v2}` and `gce_plat_v2 = {.thread_nr = 16}`; (c) MT6768's display path reaches it through the plain framework: even_defconfig has `# CONFIG_MTK_CMDQ_MBOX_EXT is not set` + `CONFIG_MTK_CMDQ_MBOX=y` (:1807/:4452), and v3's `cmdq_helper_ext.c:5367-5390` loop calls `cmdq_mbox_create(dev, i)` -> `mbox_request_channel()` (the helper, not the engine - `grep -rn mbox_request_channel drivers/misc/mediatek/cmdq/` is empty), breaking at the first failure, so the v3 24-thread request silently truncates to the provider's 16 channels; (d) `cmdqRecCreate`/`cmdqRecWrite` are thin wrappers (`v3/cmdq_record.c:3808`/`:3887`) over `cmdq_task_create`/`cmdq_op_write_reg`; (e) in OUR tree `CONFIG_MTK_CMDQ_MBOX=y` already builds both `drivers/mailbox/mtk-cmdq-mailbox.o` (123,568 B, idle - no matching compat, our node has no #mbox-cells) and `drivers/soc/mediatek/mtk-cmdq-helper.o` (104,232 B) which already defines and exports `cmdq_pkt_write_s_value` (:271) and `cmdq_pkt_write_s_mask_value` (:285, emitting `CMDQ_CODE_MASK`+`~mask` then `CMDQ_CODE_WRITE_S_MASK` = stock's pair), with the opcodes present at `include/linux/mailbox/mtk-cmdq-mailbox.h:56-65`. Conclusion: the record half no longer needs invention, but it needs an *edit to already-published patches* (0070's DT transplant: add `#mbox-cells` and a provider node; 0082's revert territory: one `cmdq_of_ids[]` line), so it is a human decision, and the three options are costed in report/gce-binding-stock-evidence.md: keep deferring (costs a link, not a behaviour), mirror stock's 3-cell topology (drags the v3 task layer back in - Option-A territory, already killed by gate 1), or translate to mainline's 2-cell binding (small, but the per-channel timeout cell disappears and `#mbox-cells` 2 vs 3 means stock's phandle args cannot be copied). Nothing was implemented; no compatible string, #mbox-cells or port-local provider was added.
decisions.still_open_on_purpose: The choice itself (options 1/2/3), and with it whether the display slice's remaining 29 cmdqRecWrite references get closed before or after the DSI/config slice. Unverified by measurement and listed as such in the report: thread-priority encoding equivalence, the effect of the ignored `default_tokens`/`max_prefetch_cnt`, whether the 24->16 thread truncation is load-bearing for any display scenario, and whether M4U/SMI remapping applies to GCE-written slot memory.
consequences: report/gce-binding-stock-evidence.md is the evidence dossier for that decision, with file:line citations for every claim.

The instruction 'resolve from stock evidence, do not speculate' is satisfied for the reading that is possible offline; the rest is device- or human-only, which the report states instead of papering over.

decisions.context: 149 queued the provider slice and named the lcm_pmic.c trap. The first implementation keyed all nine objects on obj-$(CONFIG_MTK_DISP_BRINGUP) and put -DCONFIG_MT6370_PMU_DSV=1 in lcm/Makefile: 8/8 objects, 0 errors, and the two bias names closed at the whole-tree link. decisions.title: Record layer un-deferred by the user (narrow B′), then re-scoped by stock evidence: no DT change is needed, and the engine is v3 not v2
decisions.context: 154 left 0090 (ddp_path.c) queued and asked one question, because the record layer gates everything past it: cmdqRecWrite is referenced from 2 objects 29+ times at link time, and the path slice adds cmdqRecWaitNoClear/cmdqRecSetEventToken. Four costed options were put up - keep deferring; un-defer narrow B′ as a port-local provider; bridge onto mainline's CMDQ mailbox by adding an mt6768 match and a 3-cell xlate; or stop display L2 at 0090 and take another subsystem. The answer was option 2, un-defer B′, which had been framed as reopening the 'DT surface of record stays as-is' constraint.
decisions.decision: Un-defer B′, and correct its scope before writing anything: measurement shows it needs no DT edit at all. The port's DT of record already carries stock's mailbox provider node byte-for-byte (arch/arm64/boot/dts/mediatek/mt6768.dts:1614, gce_mbox@10238000, compatible = "mediatek,mt6768-gce", #mbox-cells = <3>, clocks gce/gce-timer, verified with diff against the vendor file: identical), because the earlier DT slice copied the whole node rather than a subset of it. So the 'leave the DT alone' instruction from this round stands unmodified, and the question left over is purely driver-side. Second correction: the option text named cmdq/v2/cmdq_record.c (2,352 lines) as the provider, which is what the census's grep printed, but even_defconfig:1804 sets CONFIG_MTK_CMDQ_V3=y and drivers/misc/mediatek/cmdq/Makefile:22 adds v3/ for mt6768 only in that case - and for mt6768 the v2 fallback list does NOT include this SoC, so stock either builds v3 (4,140 lines of record code alone, 16 objects in the directory) or builds no engine at all. v2 is not the board's provider and will not be ported as a substitute for it.
decisions.still_open_on_purpose: The choice between the two remaining shapes of B′, for the next round to take with the numbers in 11.15: (i) a port-local provider, leaving mainline's mtk-cmdq-mailbox.c untouched, or (ii) an mt6768 entry in mainline's match table plus 3-cell xlate. The measured obstacle to (ii) is that stock's own drivers/mailbox/mtk-cmdq-mailbox.c cmdq_xlate consumes (thread, timeout, priority) - args[1] is a timeout that falls back to CMDQ_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT when 0, args[2] is the priority - while 5.15's cmdq_xlate reads args[1] as the priority and never looks at args[2], with no args_count check; so importing the vendor semantics into the shared xlate silently changes every other SoC's binding, and mainline's binding document describes 2 cells. Also open by design: whether the record layer can ever be exercised without hardware (section 5 of the design doc says it cannot, since nothing in the landed set calls cmdqRecCreate - the macros take their CPU branch when handle is NULL), and the rule that follows from it: an adapter must never drop a write to look green; with no channel it returns an error the caller logs.
decisions.consequences: Sequencing: 0090 (ddp_path.c, measured 78 -> 65 distinct open names) lands first and is robust to every option here, since both names it opens are closed by whichever record shape is chosen. 0091 is then the record layer itself, sized by this decision's measurements rather than by the census's grep. The bdg rewrite (ddp_disp_bdg.c:3030 and its 17 cmdq_pkt_write/_poll sites), the 14 data symbols, and videox/primary_display.c stay as they were; so does MT6370's unreachable-by-DT state, which was a separate question and is still 'leave it alone'. Expect maturity to move from 'compiles and links' to 'compiles, links, and the record API has a provider' - still not 'works', which needs a device.
